motivation: Determine whether exact-point occupancy by another seagrass after Thalassia loss reflects persistence of a pre-existing mixed-species patch rather than de novo colonization after focal loss.

source.stable_point_id: Point-event locationID constructed upstream as Transect + Site/meter-mark identity
source.seagrass_definition: Present occurrence rows in order Alismatales
source.point_year_consistency: Retain only point-years for which repeated visits agree on the complete set of present Alismatales scientificName values. Any within-year taxon-set disagreement is excluded.

primary_endpoint.eligible_transition: same stable point observed in consecutive years; source-year Thalassia present; target-year Thalassia absent; target-year has >=1 other present seagrass
primary_endpoint.source_alternative_set: all present Alismatales taxa other than Thalassia testudinum in source point-year
primary_endpoint.target_alternative_set: all present Alismatales taxa other than Thalassia testudinum in target point-year
primary_endpoint.de_novo_only_event: target_alternative_set non-empty and intersection with source_alternative_set is empty

hypothesis.statement: Most exact-point alternative-seagrass occupancy after Thalassia loss is persistence of at least one alternative species already co-occurring with Thalassia in the source year, rather than entirely de novo colonization.
hypothesis.estimator: fraction of eligible replacement events with non-empty source-target alternative-species intersection
hypothesis.support_rule: lower bound of 95% node-cluster bootstrap interval > 0.5

secondary_descriptive.by_segment: Report pre-existing persistence fraction separately for Old, Middle, and Lower Tampa Bay; do not promote a segment-specific result if the pooled primary rule fails.
secondary_descriptive.by_taxon: For each target alternative taxon, report events where that taxon persisted from source versus appeared only in target.

claim_boundary: Post-hoc ecological hypothesis motivated by the already-opened exact-point community-buffering result.
Persistence of a co-occurring alternative species is consistent with species-specific dropout from a mixed patch, not proof of facilitation or competition.
De novo appearance is an observation transition and need not imply biological colonization within one year because detection can vary.
Do not relax complete taxon-set consistency, event/node minima, period, segment pool, or the 0.5 majority threshold after opening the endpoint.
Any supported result describes point-scale community-state turnover, not equivalence of ecosystem function among species.
